title: I Enforced the PTA Snack Allergen List After the Cupcakes Appeared Anyway

parts.text: I printed the allergen list on Monday: no tree nuts, no homemade mystery frosting. Friday a tray of walnut cupcakes arrived from the snack parent, Becca, who said kids need joy. My kid has an EpiPen. I was thirty-seven. The teacher froze. I photographed the list on the cupboard, the walnuts, the sign-in. Becca said I was making her child feel bad. Then she posted in the PTA group that some parents want to ban birthdays.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She recast walnuts as a birthday ban in the PTA group.

social.video_title: The cupboard list lost to a tray of walnuts — Part 1/2
social.description: EpiPen, printed list, joy cupcakes. Then a group post. Would you have sent them home?

parts.text: I commented with the cupboard photo and the nurse policy. The cupcakes went home. Store-safe snacks arrived. Becca's child still had a birthday at actual birthday time. My kid ate a sealed granola bar and stayed breathing, which is the joy I came for. The list stayed on the cupboard. Frosting can be joyful without walnuts. The PTA group learned the difference between a ban and a label.

social.description: Sealed snacks, breathing, birthday elsewhere. Was joy an ingredient?
